newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen firm at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen firm at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open firmer on Monday, maintaining positive momentum ahead of a week full of critical economic data.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index rose 2.95 points to 947.85, while the long bond added 4/32 to 6.45 percent.

"Based on futures and bonds, I think we're headed for a firmer open," Mike Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said. "Japanese and German markets are doing better...Portfolio managers have a need to be fully invested in this market."

Technology stocks were expected to be active, after reports showing worldwide personal computer growth surged in the second quarter, and following an acquistion announcement for Chips and Technologies Inc by semiconductor company Intel Corp, analysts said.
Among this week's economic data, stock and bond markets would peruse the second quarter employment cost index, due on Tuesday, and Friday's employment report for July.
